decision.question: How does a spawned agent report to the agent that spawned it: by logging to its own session.jsonl, or by chat?
decision.ask: How does a spawned agent report to the agent that spawned it: by logging to its own session.jsonl, or by chat?

options.text: A. Log first, plain follow: spawn subscribes the parent to the child's session.jsonl (follow, default 2 s bursts); the child reports by logging; chat only for a clarification
options.say: A. Log first, plain follow: spawn subscribes the parent to the child's session.jsonl (follow, default 2 s bursts); the child reports by logging; chat only for a clarification
caveats: Every burst wakes the parent for a paid turn, and each turn re-reads its whole context: a child logging every 30 s costs the parent a turn every 30 s
The subscription outlives the child (Follow drops only the follower's own subscriptions when it stops), so dead logs stay watched
options.caveat: Every burst wakes the parent for a paid turn, and each turn re-reads its whole context: a child logging every 30 s costs the parent a turn every 30 s The subscription outlives the child (Follow drops only the follower's own subscriptions when it stops), so dead logs stay watched

options.text: B. Keep chat first, mirror to the log: the child answers in chat as today and the wake text is also appended to its session.jsonl
options.say: B. Keep chat first, mirror to the log: the child answers in chat as today and the wake text is also appended to its session.jsonl
caveats: The report still lives mainly in the parent's context window, which dies with the session
Two copies of the same report drift; the owner asked for the opposite
options.caveat: The report still lives mainly in the parent's context window, which dies with the session Two copies of the same report drift; the owner asked for the opposite

options.text: C. Log first, with brakes: the parent follows the child's session.jsonl with a 60 s gather window, the subscription ends when the child stops, the turn-end wake stays as the one 'done' signal, and the minion skill says the report goes in the log and the last words are one line pointing at it
options.say: C. Log first, with brakes: the parent follows the child's session.jsonl with a 60 s gather window, the subscription ends when the child stops, the turn-end wake stays as the one 'done' signal, and the minion skill says the report goes in the log and the last words are one line pointing at it
caveats: Still up to one extra parent turn per minute while a child logs; masterminds with many children pay for each
The wake still carries the child's last words (chat) until a later slice replaces its body with the new log lines
options.caveat: Still up to one extra parent turn per minute while a child logs; masterminds with many children pay for each The wake still carries the child's last words (chat) until a later slice replaces its body with the new log lines

decision.why: It is the owner's ask (the minion logs an overview, the parent tails it) built on the follow tool that already exists, with two brakes that stop the parent paying a turn per log line and stop dead logs being watched. A is the same idea without the brakes; B keeps the report in a context window that dies.

decision.question: How does a VS Code tab's session folder get its session.jsonl, and what goes in it?
decision.ask: How does a VS Code tab's session folder get its session.jsonl, and what goes in it?

options.text: A. Hooks write it, in the store folder: the SessionStart hook appends line 1 {session:{id, kind:'vscode-tab', cwd, at}} to ai/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/session-<id8>/session.jsonl; prompt-relay's session_page_url returns /framework/ai/sessions/<id>/ so the owner's prompts (already logged by code) land in page.jsonl BESIDE it, not in the old flat ai/YYYY/MM/DD/ folder; new-task and finish-task lines go to session.jsonl
options.say: A. Hooks write it, in the store folder: the SessionStart hook appends line 1 {session:{id, kind:'vscode-tab', cwd, at}} to ai/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/session-<id8>/session.jsonl; prompt-relay's session_page_url returns /framework/ai/sessions/<id>/ so the owner's prompts (already logged by code) land in page.jsonl BESIDE it, not in the old flat ai/YYYY/MM/DD/ folder; new-task and finish-task lines go to session.jsonl
caveats: Two files per tab (session.jsonl for events, page.jsonl for the prompt items the Echo and Refine readers expect) until the page tool can read prompts out of session.jsonl
DayPromptsRefine walks the old ai/YYYY/MM/DD tree and must learn the store path; 13 days of old prompt pages stay where they are unless a move script runs
options.caveat: Two files per tab (session.jsonl for events, page.jsonl for the prompt items the Echo and Refine readers expect) until the page tool can read prompts out of session.jsonl DayPromptsRefine walks the old ai/YYYY/MM/DD tree and must learn the store path; 13 days of old prompt pages stay where they are unless a move script runs

options.text: B. AISessionIndex writes it: when the transcript watcher first sees a session it appends line 1, and later copies each owner prompt from the transcript into session.jsonl
options.say: B. AISessionIndex writes it: when the transcript watcher first sees a session it appends line 1, and later copies each owner prompt from the transcript into session.jsonl
caveats: The watcher runs inside the dev server, main checkout only, so a tab's record depends on the site being up
Copies the prompt text a second time (the transcript and page.jsonl already hold it): text stored twice drifts
options.caveat: The watcher runs inside the dev server, main checkout only, so a tab's record depends on the site being up Copies the prompt text a second time (the transcript and page.jsonl already hold it): text stored twice drifts

options.text: C. Leave it: the store folder keeps cache.jsonl and index.json, prompts stay in the old flat folder, and readers join the two
options.say: C. Leave it: the store folder keeps cache.jsonl and index.json, prompts stay in the old flat folder, and readers join the two
caveats: The owner's rule 'every session folder has session.jsonl' stays false
Every reader keeps two places in mind; the tab's prompts are invisible from its own session page
options.caveat: The owner's rule 'every session folder has session.jsonl' stays false Every reader keeps two places in mind; the tab's prompts are invisible from its own session page

decision.why: The prompts are already logged by code (prompt-relay) at no token cost; they are only in the wrong folder. Hooks run for every tab whether or not the site is up, and nothing is copied twice. Queued as its own task because the hook and its readers belong to the session-record work in flight.
